title: Every new step is measured against every open one: queue order and what runs together
task:
Every new step is measured against every open step, for its place in the queue and for what can run beside it; the queue is re-ranked at each new step, never ordered by date. Today the kit sorts steps by train, then by date (scripts/kit.py); the priority the workstreams had on 11-20 (P1-P3, sorted) was lost on 11-22 when the train became the task list (2e74fce), and nobody noticed. On 2026-11-26 the web orchestrator launched M5 to M8 (features) while CL51 waited; CL51's bug then overwrote 11 posts. Concurrency is not measured between steps either: the split check (0eca719) looks inside one step only; between steps the guide just says "launch several at once when they do not touch the same files".

1. At `step new` (and at each resume while steps are open) the new step is compared with each open one, pair by pair, on facts: does it repair damage (data lost or wrong, found by a review, a done or the owner) or put data at risk; does the other wait on it (it changes what the other builds on, or the other would redo or undo its work); do they touch the same files or the same area of the map (M1); is one a bug in what the other builds. In scripts/kit.py.
2. From those pairs: the queue order (damage first; then what unblocks the most steps; then bugs before features; date only to break a tie), and the running sets: two steps that share files or an area never run at the same time; the later one waits, named.
3. Every new step re-ranks the whole queue; resume and `kit.py queue` show it with one line of why for each place ("before M2: M2 builds on the format this fixes"); the orchestrator launches from its top, and a launch out of order is refused with the step that should go first named (`--anyway "<why>"` records it).
4. A step already running that a new P1 step would undo or redo gets a message to pause at its next save point.
5. Tests on a fixture board: a new damage step goes to the top; a step that two others wait on goes before them; two steps on the same file never both run; a launch out of order is refused.
verdict: Yes: the queue is re-ranked at every new step and every resume, a reason on each line; same-file steps never run together; an out-of-order launch is refused, naming the step to launch first.
bars: 7 of 7 checks pass on a fixture board (the 7th: questions and issues filed under a train are not steps): a repair goes to the top and pauses the running step it would undo, a step two others wait on goes first, a bug comes before a feature on its files, two same-file steps never both run, an out-of-order launch is refused and the override is recorded, and a new step re-ranks the queue

this board (anlonlt/board) today: 25 of 25 open steps ranked (26 before the fix: the question cl27-q-trains-view was counted); 10 of 25 running, 9 of 25 can start now, 6 of 25 wait with the blocking step named. On Harmonize the orchestrator counted 17 steps, and its questions (F5, VR5, HL5, O56) were ranked until this fix
0 of the 26 live steps are marked as repairs by their wording: CL51 would need `--damage` to go first (the reason for the flag)
76 of 77 suites pass in the full run after merging main (CL49); the one that fails, tests/test_cl48_test_guard.py, fails the same on origin/main alone
breaks: sed -i 's/    damage = bool(q.get("damage")) or bool(said)/    damage = False/' scripts/kit.py
not_checked: the real 11-26 replay (M5 to M8 against CL51) on the board as it was then: the fixture test reproduces its shape, not the posts themselves
the agy orchestrator path (`invoke_subagent`): it does not go through `kit.py launch`, so the order check only reaches it through the guide and resume
